title: Measurable competence
loopType: Reinforcing loop that shifts joy from self-directed exploration toward performance.
interventionOpportunities: Parent-facing design that values boredom and experimentation

title: Play becomes proof
interventionOpportunities: Portfolio systems that preserve process and private experimentation
Youth spaces not organized around achievement
Education policy that protects arts and recess as ends in themselves

title: Productivity ratchet
interventionOpportunities: Organizational norms around workload and AI
Playful workplace spaces not tied to output
Designs that mark recovery as legitimate

title: Extrinsic-reward displacement
loopType: Reward conditioning → motivational displacement → reinforcing loop.
notes: Grades, praise, points, money, likes, rankings, and workplace metrics make action legible and socially rewarded.
People learn to prioritize what can be counted or displayed.
Their attention can shift away from curiosity, process, and internal satisfaction.
Reduced access to intrinsically motivated activity makes reward systems feel increasingly necessary.
evidenceAnchor: Anticipated and contingent tangible rewards can undermine free-choice intrinsic motivation for otherwise interesting activities; feedback is different when it is informational rather than controlling.

title: Time scarcity and depleted play
loopType: Structural pressure → depletion → convenience substitution → reinforcing loop.
notes: This loop is central to the “Joy Deficit.”
It shows why telling individuals to “play more” is insufficient: depleted time, attention, money, and public space are systemic constraints.

title: Play-to-productivity capture
notes: A game becomes a ranked competition.
A restorative behavior becomes a wellness metric.
designQuestion: How could an object preserve the boundary between play and proof?

title: Social play as restoration
loopType: Enabling condition → social reinforcement → regenerative loop. The primary counter-loop.
notes: It turns joy from a private consumer experience into shared social infrastructure.
